name: Crucible UGL-2 'Understudy'
description:
A single-shot underslung grenade launcher designed to mount beneath the barrel of any standard assault rifle or carbine via universal rail adapter. The UGL-2 adds grenade capability to a primary weapon system without requiring the operator to carry a dedicated launcher, trading capacity for convenience. The break-action loading mechanism accepts standard 40mm casings and can be reloaded in under three seconds by a trained operator.

Crucible designed the Understudy for squad-level operations where dedicated grenade launchers are impractical — room clearing, vehicle patrols, and quick-reaction scenarios where switching between primary weapon and launcher would cost critical seconds. The universal rail adapter fits 94% of assault platforms currently in production, making it the default choice for operators who want explosive capability without the weight penalty of a standalone launcher.
legality: Military — restricted; Licensed for corporate security with explosive ordnance permit
specifications: caliber: 40mm standard casings capacity: 1 round effective range: 50-350 meters weight: 1.8 kg length: 305mm mounting: Universal accessory rail
tactical_use: Squad-level explosive support. Operators carry 4-6 rounds in belt pouches and reload between engagements. Used primarily for breaching reinforced doors, disabling vehicles, and flushing targets from cover.
cultural_context: The Understudy is so common in GLMZ's security ecosystem that 'checking for understudies' has become standard practice when disarming a suspect — the launcher sits flush beneath a rifle barrel and can be missed on visual inspection if you're not looking for it.
known_users: Corporate security teams across all major corponations
story_hooks: A batch of UGL-2 launchers has been modified to fire a proprietary 40mm round that deploys a localized EMP on detonation — turning a common infantry attachment into a cyberware killer.
An operator's Understudy misfired during a corporate raid, sending a fragmentation round into a residential floor. Crucible claims manufacturing defect. The operator claims the weapon was sabotaged.
related_entities: Arcturus Defense Solutions Kinetic Echo Harness — 'The Understudy'

physical_description.visual_profile: Compact, utilitarian single-shot launcher with a distinctly modular appearance. The break-action breech dominates the profile—a pronounced hinge mechanism that opens vertically. Underslung orientation makes it appear almost like a secondary tool grafted onto a primary weapon. Minimal ornamentation; all design language is functional and industrial.
physical_description.dimensions: 305mm overall length, 85mm width at widest point (breech assembly), 60mm height excluding mounting bracket. Barrel bore: 40mm.
physical_description.weight_description: Hefty but balanced—1.8kg feels anchored in the hand, substantial enough to demand respect but not cumbersome when underslung. The recoil dampener system gives it a slightly soft, dampened feel during handling.
physical_description.primary_material: Steel barrel and breech assembly; reinforced polymer receiver housing with carbon-composite reinforcement at stress points. Universal rail mounting bracket is hardened aluminum alloy.
physical_description.finish: Matte black powder coat on steel components, slightly worn at edges from field use. Polymer receiver has a slightly textured, non-reflective finish with minor scuff marks. Aluminum bracket shows brushed metal with light oxidation.
physical_description.color_scheme: Matte black primary with gunmetal gray aluminum accents on the rail adapter and breech lever. No accent colors—pure utilitarian monochrome.
physical_description.grip_texture: The firing lever is stippled polymer with fine crosshatching for positive grip in gloved or wet conditions. The reload knob on the breech hinge is knurled steel, cold to the touch.
distinctive_features: Vertical break-action hinge with oversized lever—mechanical and deliberately obvious
Three parallel cooling ribs running along the barrel shroud
Recessed loading port designed for rapid magazine-style ammunition insertion
Pressure relief vent ports along the receiver sidewalls
Integrated witness marks (tiny etched lines) on the breech showing charge status
Mounting bracket has quick-detach pins rather than screws—field-expedient removal
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: CRUCIBLE INDUSTRIAL stamp on the left side of the receiver, just forward of the trigger guard. Small serial number plate (approximately 2cm × 1cm) mounted on the underside of the barrel, deliberately hidden from casual view. Model designation 'UGL-2' etched in small letters on the breech lever itself.
physical_description.condition_typical: Well-maintained working weapon. The matte finish shows light wear at the mounting points and breech hinge from repeated loading cycles. No rust or corrosion, but carbon scoring visible around the muzzle. Mounting bracket shows witness marks from rail contact. This is a tool, not a display piece.
